findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer solution to be testing at 0 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was remade and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure sanitizer solution is prepared and available at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Garbage and refuse are properly disposed; facilities are maintained.
findings.comment: Observed refuse in trash cans to be overflowing onto floor in kitchen. Discussed with PIC, trash cans was emptied and waste was removed. Ensure refuse is removed from facility at a frequency that prevents buildup from occurring.
findings.citation_text: 5-502.11 Frequency. REFUSE, recyclables, and returnables shall be removed from the PREMISES at a frequency that will minimize the development of objectionable odors and other conditions that attract or harbor insects and rodents.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the dish machine to have 0 ppm of bleach. Facility had just opened for summer camp this week and the sanitizing agent likely has yet to be changed out from last summer. Discussed with staff. GFS services the dish machine per the sticker on the side of the equipment. Contact GFS to service the machine. Facility has bleach test strips. Ensure test strip use to verify bleach concentrations - 50 to 200 ppm. Inspector instructed staff to use the 3 compartment sink until the dish machine is fixed - wash, rinse, sanitize. Inspector will follow-up on 6/20/23 (6/19 is a holiday).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the dish machine to have a leak at the base with a container catching the water. This was noted during the last routine inspection in July of 2022 (general comments area). Discussed with staff. Ensure the machine is repaired before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no active sani bucket upon start of the inspection. Staff was mid-cooking lunch already. Discussed with staff. Ensure a sani bucket is made prior to engaging in food manipulation. PIC made a bleach bucket - 200 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Caulking is needed in the following areas: kitchen hand sink to wall (missing), back splash of the 3 compartment sink area (splash to wall and at the base of the splash where the counter meets it), dish machine to wall (missing all around), women’s bathroom (coming away from sink and wall). Re-caulk/caulk the above areas so they are smooth and easily cleanable.
2. Men’s bathroom has dry wall tears and the wall is no longer smooth and easily cleanable above the hand sinks.
3. Coving is coming away from around the perimeter of the dry storage area particularly against the walk-in freezer - reseal the coving.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

No reporting agreements or other verifiable documentation are available for food employees related to foodborne illnesses. A copy of the SCDPH reporting agreement was given to the PIC and they were filled out during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

On arrival, no written procedure is available for cleaning up vomit/diarrhea at the facility. PIC is aware of the needed procedure (conducted by the janitor). The procedure was reviewed during the inspection and the inspector will leave a copy of the procedure SCDPH acquired from the CDC’s website.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the dish machine would not effect a noticeable change on the inspector's test strips. The jug of sanitizer is observed clear as apposed to the yellowish color of jugs in storage and was opened during the winter (per the PIC). The jug was replace and the machine primed with the new jug. Concentration is now showing in the 50-100 ppm range.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 (P) FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

Multiple condiments in the reach in cooler were observed with mold growth on the containers. Mold was also observed on the lid of a container of pickles and in a container of sour cream. The sour cream and the condiments were discarded during the inspection and the PIC was instructed to clean the lid of the pickle container. The PIC was also instructed to clean the reach in cooler to ensure any mold spores are removed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

Observed the microwave in the dinning room to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1210e  Equipment attached to walls and ceilings shall be easily clean able and shall be maintained in good repair.

Observed a crack in the seam between the mop sink and wall on the left of the sink. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to repair and maintain walls and attached equipment.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
Observed several ceiling tiles to have water damage and others to be missing. While discussing with the PIC it was stated that there were some frozen pipes that caused issues an that someone is already scheduled to repair and replace the damaged tiles prior to the facility opening for its summer season.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million. Observed no test kit on site during inspection. PC said thst it would be aquired in the future.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration. Observed dish machine at 0 ppm cl during inspection. Maintenance guy arrived and repaired during inspection. Machine now at 50 ppm cl.
